_comment: Skill pairs that score as near-duplicates but are legitimately distinct.
Add a pair here ONLY after reading both descriptions and confirming a real
difference in scope, platform, or offense-vs-defense posture. The 'reason'
is not bookkeeping: it is the wording each skill's negative trigger should
use, e.g. reason 'Linux vs Windows' becomes 'Do not use for Windows hosts
A pair that is genuinely ambiguous does NOT belong here. Disambiguate the
Regenerate the candidate list with: python tools/detect-collisions.py

reviewed_distinct.reason: Same CIS Benchmark methodology, different operating systems. The controls, tooling and audit commands do not overlap, so both must exist; each description must name the OS explicitly and point at the other.

Same PDF-triage toolset, different primary tool and depth: pdfid centers on rapid structure/keyword triage and attack-vector classification, peepdf on deep interactive object and JavaScript/shellcode extraction; each description points triage work at pdfid and deep extraction at peepdf.

Both use Sigstore Cosign, but cosign skill targets container image provenance with Kubernetes admission-control enforcement while sigstore skill targets general software/binary artifact signing in CI/CD; each negative trigger names the other's scope.

Different telemetry: sysmon skill detects via Sysmon Event IDs 1/11 correlated with parent processes, while the hunt works Windows Security Event 4698 task-creation records; each description names the other's data source.

Opposite posture on the same platforms: review skill assesses/identifies serverless misconfigurations, securing skill implements hardening controls (least-privilege IAM, secrets, runtime monitoring); each points assessment vs implementation at the other.

Same GoPhish tool, different interface: simulation skill is manual admin-panel campaign setup, red-team skill automates campaigns via the Python gophish library; each description points the other interface elsewhere.

Different tool version: CE skill targets BloodHound Community Edition (Docker/graph-database deployment), the other the legacy/classic BloodHound; each negative trigger names the edition it is not for.
Different tool version: analyzing skill uses classic Volatility (v2) across Windows/Linux/macOS, conducting skill uses Volatility 3; each description names the other framework version.
Different tool version: analyzing skill uses classic Volatility (v2) across Windows/Linux/macOS, the other uses the Volatility 3 framework; each description names the other framework version.
Tool-specific vs general technique: impacket skill is Impacket GetUserSPNs.py-specific, the other is a tool-agnostic Kerberoasting methodology; each negative trigger routes the other case away.

Different method: attack skill is broad ATT&CK behavior/IOC mapping and intel reporting across Enterprise/Mobile/ICS matrices, navigator skill specifically generates ATT&CK Navigator layer files via attackcti; each points the other scope away.

Different execution framework for Atomic Red Team: purple-team skill uses Invoke-AtomicRedTeam (PowerShell) with Sigma correlation and detection-validation loops, the other uses the atomic-operator Python framework; each names the other framework.

Both use CHIPSEC, opposite posture: bootkit skill analyzes UEFI malware/persistence families (BlackLotus, LoJax, MoonBounce), auditing skill assesses platform firmware configuration and protections (SPI write protection, BIOS lock, SMM); each names the other's focus.

Different scope: gatekeeper skill is Kubernetes admission-control mechanics alone (ConstraintTemplates, mutation, deny at admission), policy-as-code skill is OPA policy-as-code spanning CI/CD pipelines as well as Kubernetes; each names the other's scope.

Different tool/method for CT-log monitoring: phishing skill uses Certstream real-time streaming for organization-targeted phishing, the other uses crt.sh/pycrtsh querying with Levenshtein typosquatting and shadow-IT detection; each names the other's method.

Client vs server: feed-integration skill builds a Python STIX/TAXII client to poll and parse feeds with the stix2 library, the other deploys and operates a TAXII server with OpenTAXII/Medallion in Docker; each names the other's role.

Narrow task vs full engagement: cracking skill does offline WPA/WPA2 passphrase cracking of a captured handshake, the other is a full wireless penetration test (rogue AP, segmentation, evil twin); each routes the other scope away.

Different focus/tooling on Modbus: injection skill detects command-injection and malformed-frame attacks with ICS-aware IDS/DPI, the other does general statistical traffic-anomaly baselining with pymodbus/Scapy/Zeek; each names the other's scope.

Tool-specific vs general: splunk skill is Splunk-SPL-specific, the other is SIEM-agnostic multi-source detection spanning network flow and endpoint telemetry; each negative trigger routes the other case away.
Different method/platform: dns-query-analysis skill uses passive-DNS statistical/ML detection, the other analyzes Zeek dns.log; each names the other's method.

Signing/enforcement vs verification: cosign skill signs images and enforces verified-images-only at Kubernetes admission, the other verifies SLSA provenance with slsa-verifier against build levels; each names the other's role.
Different telemetry: sysmon skill detects via Sysmon Event IDs 1/11 correlated with parent processes, the hunt works Windows Security Event 4698 via SIEM/EDR; each names the other's data source.
Different method: dns-query-analysis skill uses passive-DNS log monitoring with statistical/ML methods, the other uses scapy-based live packet-capture analysis; each names the other's method.
General vs tool-specific: executing skill is a tool-agnostic phishing-simulation methodology, the other is GoPhish-specific campaign setup and reporting; each routes the other case away.

Artifact forensics vs log hunting: malware-artifacts skill investigates the trojanized artifacts/samples themselves, the other runs a SIEM/EDR log-based threat hunt for supply-chain compromise; each names the other's approach.
Different method/platform: dns-query-analysis skill uses passive-DNS statistical/ML detection, the other analyzes Zeek dns.log; each names the other's method.

Different artifact: beacon-configuration skill extracts embedded config from Beacon PE files/memory dumps, the other parses Malleable C2 profile definitions (AST) and builds traffic detections; each names the other's input.
Investigation vs detection engineering: analyzing skill investigates incidents and reconstructs timelines in Splunk, the other authors SPL detection/correlation rules; each names the other's task.
Same AFL++ tool, different context: cicd skill integrates fuzzing into a CI/CD pipeline, the other runs standalone campaigns with corpus minimization and crash triage; each names the other's context.

Same Suricata tool, different mode: monitoring skill is passive IDS detection, EVE logging, SIEM integration and file extraction, the other is inline IPS (NFQueue) focused on actively blocking traffic; each names the other's mode.
Scope: conducting skill is general/internal network penetration testing, the other is a dedicated external/internet-facing perimeter test; each routes the other scope away.
Different platform: dns-logs skill does SIEM-based DNS-log analysis with DGA detection, the other analyzes Zeek dns.log specifically; each names the other's platform.
